title: Recognizing Signs of Missed Miscarriage in Pregnancy
excerpt: Missed miscarriage occurs when a fetus dies in the womb but is not expelled.
content:
## Summary
Missed miscarriage, also known as missed abortion, is a condition where the fetus dies in the womb but is not expelled. This can be a devastating experience for expectant mothers, and it's essential to recognize the signs and symptoms to seek medical care promptly. Unlike a typical miscarriage, where the fetus is expelled from the body, a missed miscarriage occurs when the fetus remains in the uterus. It's crucial to understand the differences between a missed miscarriage and other pregnancy complications to ensure proper care and support.

## Practical tips
To recognize the signs of a missed miscarriage, it's essential to be aware of the common symptoms. These may include a decrease or complete stop of fetal movement, vaginal bleeding or spotting, severe abdominal pain or cramping, and a decrease in pregnancy symptoms such as morning sickness or breast tenderness. Additionally, some women may experience a loss of pregnancy glow or a feeling of being unwell. If you're experiencing any of these symptoms, it's crucial to seek medical care promptly. In the meantime, prioritize your health by eating a balanced diet, staying hydrated, and getting plenty of rest. Avoid taking any medication or supplements without consulting your healthcare provider.

## When to seek care
If you're experiencing any of the following symptoms, seek medical care immediately: severe abdominal pain or cramping, heavy vaginal bleeding, fever, difficulty breathing, or fainting. Additionally, if you notice a significant decrease in fetal movement, especially after 28 weeks of gestation, seek medical attention right away. It's also essential to attend regular prenatal check-ups to monitor your health and the health of your baby.

## FAQs
Q1: What is the difference between a missed miscarriage and a typical miscarriage?
A1: A missed miscarriage occurs when the fetus dies in the womb but is not expelled, whereas a typical miscarriage is when the fetus is expelled from the body.
Q2: What are the common symptoms of a missed miscarriage?
A2: Common symptoms include a decrease or complete stop of fetal movement, vaginal bleeding or spotting, severe abdominal pain or cramping, and a decrease in pregnancy symptoms.
Q3: How can I prioritize my health during pregnancy to reduce the risk of complications?
A3: Prioritize your health by eating a balanced diet, staying hydrated, getting plenty of rest, and attending regular prenatal check-ups. Avoid taking any medication or supplements without consulting your healthcare provider, and seek medical care promptly if you experience any concerning symptoms.
